ass="el49-kicker">06 · Comparable Systems and Precedents

Evidence for the mechanism—not validation of this map

Earthline’s intervention logic is consistent with long-standing landscape systems that slow runoff, increase residence time, retain sediment and support vegetation. These cases demonstrate mechanisms. They do not validate the location, dimensions or performance of any corridor in this report.

${precedents()}
Claim boundary. Comparable systems justify investigating the mechanism. Only local observation, survey, soil testing, monitored implementation and blind validation can establish Earthline performance.
${footer(data,'06')}
07 · Data Gaps and Their Significance

What is missing—and whether it changes the decision

${gapRows(d)}
Material consequence: the missing inputs prevent construction placement and most quantitative impact claims. They do not erase the regional finding that certain landform positions deserve closer investigation.
${footer(data,'07')}
08 · Conclusions and Recommended Next Step

Move from regional screening to defensible project evidence

${esc(next)}

1 · Select

Choose a smaller project area around one or more priority corridors. Preserve the original regional run identity for traceability.

2 · Verify terrain

Use bare-earth LiDAR/DTM or survey-grade contours. Do not infer detailed grade from canopy-top or building-top elevation.

3 · Verify water and exclusions

Confirm mapped and field-observed channels, structures, roads, driveways, utilities and safe overflow.

4 · Verify soils

Complete infiltration testing and soil-profile review. Apply the 48-hour drawdown method to the verified corridor position.

5 · Design ecology and maintenance

Select locally appropriate vegetation, access, sediment forebays, inspection and long-term maintenance responsibilities.

6 · Monitor

Document as-built geometry and observe water levels, overflow, sediment, vegetation and maintenance after storms.

${footer(data,'08')}
${howBioswalesReportPages16388(data)} ${EARTHLINE_CORRECTIONS_REGISTRY_16513}
09 · Limitations and Reliance

Conditions of use

  • This report presents screening results generated by the Earthline search engine from remotely sensed terrain, mapped contextual data and rule-based hydrologic screening. It is not an engineering design, construction document, geotechnical investigation, survey, permit, environmental assessment, title opinion or physical site assessment.
  • Regional and Focus outputs are opportunity corridors or candidate reaches. Exact swale locations are prohibited above Property tier.
  • Terrain, hydrography, soils, rainfall, land cover, exclusions and aquifer evidence carry independent source versions and limitations.
  • Camera-scoped NOAA GRACE and WRI Aqueduct rasters are visual context only and are excluded from report findings.
  • Absence of mapped aquifer geometry is never interpreted as absence of groundwater.
  • Pre-DTM corridor-specific drawdown verdicts, storage, earthworks and recharge estimates remain provisional because corridor position and contributing area may change.
  • Qualified local professionals and field verification are required before implementation.
Reliance. Earthline search-engine results may support screening, prioritization and scoping of further work. It may not be relied upon for construction, regulatory compliance, financing-grade engineering quantities or performance guarantees.

Design consequence. When macropores stay air-filled but frozen, rapid recharge occurs. Under high antecedent soil moisture, pore ice blocks the macropores and enhances runoff instead — and infiltrated water that refreezes inside a channel will not clear until the whole frozen layer disappears. A swale saturated going into freeze-up performs worse than one that drains. This argues for depth and drainage, not capture alone.

Climate direction. In snowmelt-dominated watersheds, 100-year peak daily streamflow is projected to rise 10–30% by the 2080s, with peak timing shifting up to a month earlier. (modeled — VIC, 20 Midwestern watersheds) Earlier, sharper melt is precisely what distributed retention buffers.

6.4 · Water quality — and why slope position decides it

Two independent mechanisms make the same volume of recharge cleaner when it enters high on a slope.

Contributing area. Water intercepted near the top of a slope has crossed less ground and had fewer opportunities to contact a road, a barnyard, a septic field, or a fertilized acre. Nitrogen available for leaching is directly related to impervious cover in the contributing watershed.

Vadose zone thickness. Upslope positions generally have a deeper unsaturated zone. More soil column means more attenuation before water reaches the water table. Suspended solids and particle-bound pollutants — most metals — are readily removed by filtration on the way down.

Measured removal, where filtration applies:

  • Total suspended solids reduced 65–71% and zinc 30–60% in grassed swales along a highway median. (measured — Stagge and Davis, 2006)
  • Load reduction exceeded concentration reduction in a 50-asset meta-analysis — meaning most water quality benefit comes from retaining water at all, not from filtering it. (measured — global meta-analysis of field studies, 2025)
